reason: The cited evidence strongly supports the synthesis, anti-CO poisoning mechanism, and durability of HEASA-Pt for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR). However, the hypothesis extends these findings to a completely different application (automotive exhaust with H2O, NO, thermal aging) without any cited evidence that the same mechanisms apply or that the catalyst is stable and active under those specific conditions. This key premise of transferability is unsupported.
premises: Single-atom Pt sites can be stabilized within a high-entropy alloy lattice.
The high-entropy matrix synergistically modifies the electronic structure of Pt sites to weaken CO adsorption.
Weakened CO adsorption prevents poisoning and maintains activity.
The HEASA-Pt design provides high durability over long-term operation.
These benefits (anti-CO poisoning, high activity, durability) are transferable from methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) to automotive exhaust conditions (gasoline/hybrid, low-T, H2O, NO).
